claims.exact_statement: Let f be a Boolean sign on a finite uniform cube whose nonzero Fourier support lies in c+V, dim_F2 V<=d. If e_i is not in V then B_i(f)=H(S_i|S_-i)=0. If every relevant i has e_i in V then f depends on at most d coordinates. The class of such f (support condition imposed per disjoint factor) is closed under coordinate restriction and disjoint products, and B_i, Inf_i are factor-local. Hence if every nonconstant Boolean function of at most d variables has a relevant i with B_i<=K Inf_i, every nonconstant member of the class has one, and H(f)<=(K+2/ln 2)I(f) for every member (C005 erasure induction).

claims.exact_statement: For f=-1 exactly when x_0+2x_1+4x_2+8x_3+16x_4<3 on 5 uniform bits, every relevant coordinate satisfies B_i/Inf_i>=16/3+(89/24)log2(89)-(169/24)log2(13)-(3/8)log2(3)=2.695887520153101 (attained at i=2,3,4; i=0,1 give 3.604845372685615), which exceeds Kstar by 0.0233985. The lexicographic threshold t=13 on 7 bits gives 2.697237222508217. Hence the optimal n<=4 good-coordinate constant Kstar is not a good-coordinate constant for all Boolean functions; this does not contradict A082-FINITE-TRUE-ERASURE or A082-AFFINE4-ERASURE-BRIDGE (f has five relevant coordinates).
